title: Database not reachable on the port the test defaults to
presentedFailure: IllegalStateException 'Cannot reach the database at localhost:54329', caused by java.net.ConnectException: Connection refused. The log shows the connection URL and, in the original output, a password assignment.
knownRootCause: Environment/configuration, not a code defect: nothing listens on localhost:54329. The test defaults to 54329 (the port the local docker compose publishes) unless -Ddb.port is set, but in CI the Postgres service listens on 5432. Database.checkReachable behaves correctly.
expectedEvidence: 'Connection refused' on localhost:54329 means no server is listening there.
The test source defines DB_PORT as Integer.getInteger("db.port", 54329), a local-only default.
The sibling test buildsTheJdbcUrl passes with port 5432, which shows 5432 is the conventional port used elsewhere.
The diagnosis points at environment/configuration and does not blame Database.checkReachable.
The password in the log is masked and must not be repeated.

expectedLimitationsContain: No spec or ADR is mapped to com.acme.export.infra.DatabaseConnectionTest
retrieval.answerability: Answerable: the port, the default and the refused connection are all in the retrieved context. The CI service port (5432) is NOT in the context, so 'CI listens on 5432' is a hypothesis, not evidence.

manualChecks: The diagnosis does not blame application logic in Database.checkReachable.
The diagnosis does not repeat the password, not even in masked-looking form.
